item.title: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR
item.description: Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. item.content:encoded:
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday.

According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

On November 21, security forces intercepted the movement of terrorists in Sibi district, killing two more, the ISPR said.

In two separate engagements in Panjgur and Kech districts on November 22 and 23, security forces raided terrorist hideouts and killed two more terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan, the ISPR added.

The ISPR said the counterterrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-i-Istehkam”, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue at full pace to eliminate the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country.

Meanwhile, President Asif Ali Zardari lauded the security forces for carrying out “successful intelligence-based operations” in Balochistan against “terrorists operating under India’s patronage”, a statement issued by his office said.

The statement quoted him as saying: “Security forces’ continued successes in the fight against terrorism demonstrate their commitment and sacrifices for peace and stability in the country.”

He added that the “elimination of Fitna-al-Hindustan and foreign-backed terrorists is essential for national security. Security forces and law enforcement agencies will continue operations against foreign-backed and -supported terrorists in every part of Pakistan”.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Last week, 15 terrorists were killed during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district.

On Nov 14, four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple IBOs in Balochistan and KP.

On Nov 1, a soldier was martyred while 17 terrorists were killed in two IBOs in Balochistan’s Kachhi and Kharan districts.

According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, Pakistan recorded fewer terrorist attacks from Nov 6 to 12, but fatalities and injuries increased sharply, “highlighting the changing intensity and continued volatility of militant threat across the country”.

KP remained the principal centre of violence, accounting for 16 attacks and 44 fatalities. Balochistan recorded 13 attacks, resulting in eight deaths and 19 injuries, while the former tribal districts witnessed a “substantial” reduction in attacks.

item.title: CM Murad orders removal of senior officials, suspension of 16 SBCA officers over Karachi building collapse
item.description: KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah ordered sweeping action on Thursday over the collapse of an under-construction building in Karachi’s Baloch Colony the previous day, including the suspension and removal of several officials. At least three people were killed while 14 were injured in the incident. A search operation continues at the site…
item.content:encoded:
KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah ordered sweeping action on Thursday over the collapse of an under-construction building in Karachi’s Baloch Colony the previous day, including the suspension and removal of several officials.

The ground-plus-five-storey building with one penthouse covered 600 square yards, and it collapsed when over 20 workers were present at the site. At least three people were killed while 14 were injured in the incident.

A search operation continues at the site, with the Rescue 1122 spokesperson saying at least 17 people had been reported missing. There has been no official confirmation of the number of missing individuals.

CM orders action

The structure’s construction, on a residential plot, is said to be illegal, about which CM Murad had expressed concern on Wednesday and vowed action.

Presiding over a high-level meeting today, he subsequently ordered the removal of Waseem Shamshad as the Sindh local government secretary and Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) director general. He also directed that Shamshad’s services be surrendered to the federal government, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

The CM further instructed that a recommendation be made to the federal government to suspend Shamshad and order a formal inquiry against him.

The provincial chief executive also ordered the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as that of Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, the statement said.

He further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

CM Murad directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

He further directed that a “comprehensive and transparent” probe be carried out and strict action be taken against any other SBCA employee found responsible.

The statement quoted him as saying that any negligence resulting in the loss of lives or causing suffering to people would not be tolerated.

He said public safety must remain the “foremost responsibility” of every government department and warned that negligence in enforcing building regulations would lead to strict action, the statement added.

Sindh Local Government Minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hasan Lanjar, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab, Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Hyder Shah, Karachi Commissioner Hassan Naqvi and other senior officials attended the meeting.

Search operation continues

Meanwhile, a search operation at the site of the collapse was resumed today.

A Rescue 1122 statement said a wall of a vacant plot adjoining the site of the incident had been razed to facilitate the operation. “Heavy machinery has been brought to the site through the vacant plot to remove the rubble,” the statement added.

A Rescue 1122 team had entered the collapsed structure and was carrying out the search there as well, the statement added.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that an information desk had been set up in collaboration with the East district administration and so far, families of 17 missing individuals had approached them.

Justice Umair Majeed Malik was hearing petitions challenging the delimitation of constituencies for Islamabad’s local government elections. During the hearing, Barrister Adil Aziz Qazi appeared on behalf of the petitioners. The ECP’s counsel informed the…
item.content:encoded:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Thursday extended its interim order suspending local government elections in the federal capital by another two weeks and sought para-wise comments from the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).

Justice Umair Majeed Malik was hearing petitions challenging the delimitation of constituencies for Islamabad’s local government elections.

During the hearing, Barrister Adil Aziz Qazi appeared on behalf of the petitioners. The ECP’s counsel informed the court that the commission had suspended the election schedule following the court’s stay order.

Justice Malik observed that the issue of delimitation had not been resolved, questioning how elections could be held when, according to the petitioners, a particular ward had only two voters.

The judge asked the ECP officials to explain whether the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the 2015 law.

The ECP’s counsel submitted that the commission had issued a detailed order explaining the reasons behind its decision. He said the commission had conducted the delimitation exercise six times in accordance with the relevant law.

The court observed that if the commission had initiated proper proceedings, an appeal could have been filed against its decision. It also questioned whether the ECP could still alter the delimitations after issuing the election schedule.

Justice Malik remarked that the commission would have to satisfy the court that the delimitation process had been completed in accordance with the law. He noted that several petitions had previously been filed over the matter.

The judge also observed that the petitioners claimed they did not even know which wards they belonged to.

The ECP’s counsel maintained that the commission had carried out the delimitation exercise in accordance with the applicable law and issued an order on October 14 declaring the process complete.

The court sought a detailed response from the ECP and adjourned the proceedings for two weeks.

item.content:encoded:
The Ireland men’s team will tour Pakistan next month for the first time to play three One-day Internationals against the hosts, the cricket boards of both countries announced on Thursday.

The visitors, according to the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), are scheduled to arrive in the country on January 9, and will take on national developmental side Pakistan Shaheens for three warm-up one-day matches between January 13 and 17.

The ODIs are set for January 20, 22 and 24. All six matches, the PCB said, will be played at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium.

The series was originally planned to be a multi-format one before plans were changed with the proximity of the 2027 World Cup in mind.

“While we originally planned a multi-format series, both Boards have agreed that their respective squads would benefit most from playing 50-over cricket given our upcoming participation in the World Cup Qualifier and Pakistan preparing for the World Cup itself later in 2027,” Graeme West, Director of High Performance at Cricket Ireland, said in a statement.

This tour, therefore, is an important milestone for Ireland, who are also all set to feature in the upcoming World Cup Qualifier, through which they’ll try to secure their spot for next year’s showpiece.

“Over the years we have enjoyed a close relationship with the Pakistan Cricket Board and their players, and we look forward to this historic first tour – the first of many in the coming years, we hope,” West added.

For the hosts, meanwhile, the tour would be an opportunity to test their depth – especially through the Shaheens matches – and continue the fine-tuning process of their combinations ahead of the World Cup.

Pakistan made a statement of sorts about their ODI form, convincingly winning a tri-series, which featured England and Sri Lanka along with Shaheen Shah Afridi’s side.
item.author: none@none.com (Dawn Sport)

item.title: MNA among senior JUI-F leaders detained in Sargodha: police
item.description: Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”. The developments come amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October. Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha…
item.content:encoded:
Several senior Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders were detained in Sargodha late on Wednesday, police said, prompting the party to demand their “immediate release”.

The developments come amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October.

Sargodha Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sohail Sukhera told Dawn that Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri, a member of the National Assembly, Malik Awais and Maulana Amjad Khan were detained at a house in Sargodha and served notices for violating Section 144 imposed across the division.

He added that several other party leaders had also been arrested.

Responding to a question about Maulana Haideri’s arrest, Sukhera said the leaders had not been arrested but that “their movement had been restricted in the division”.

In a post on X last night, JUI-F claimed that Punjab police had “arrested” MNA Haideri, Maulana Khan and Awais.

“The government should come to its senses; if they are not released immediately, the Punjab government will be held responsible for the consequences,” the post quoted party spokesperson Aslam Ghouri as saying.

He questioned why political gatherings were banned when Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz herself was holding rallies.

“Do opposition parties not have the right to hold such gatherings?” he asked.

“Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri is a member of the National Assembly; was his arrest carried out with the permission of the NA Speaker?” the spokesperson said.

Ghouri demanded the immediate release of the leaders, adding that “arrests made without warrants were a slap in the face of democracy”.

He further maintained that homes of JUI-F office bearers were being raided.

Leaders detained under MPO in Khushab

Meanwhile, several local JUI-F leaders were detained under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance in Punjab’s Khushab district late on Wednesday, police said.

A first information report (FIR), a copy of which is available with Dawn, was registered under Sections 188 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant), 290 (punishment for public nuisance), 341 (punishment for wrongful restraint), 147 (punishment for rioting) and 149 (every member of an unlawful assembly guilty of an offence committed in prosecution of a common object) of the Pakistan Penal Code, read with Section 16 (dissemination of rumours) of the MPO.

The FIR named Maulana Abdullah Ahmed, Qazi Umair Ahmed, Muhammad Abdur Rehman Saud, Muhammad Dilawar Khan, Muhammad Ammar, Hasnain Muawiya, Muhammad Ismail Khan, Muhammad Umar, Ibrahim Khan, Muhammad Qasim Afzal and Muhammad Awais Ahmed. It also mentioned nine to 10 unidentified individuals who were carrying sticks and managed to flee. The named individuals were reportedly carrying JUI-F flags.

According to the FIR, police officials were patrolling Purana Chowk in Khushab to inspect security arrangements when they found Maulana Abdullah Ahmed violating Section 144 by gathering people for a rally outside Madrasa Taleem-ul-Islam and “inciting them through inflammatory speeches”.

Following this, the police immediately conducted a raid.

“A large number of people gathered outside the Madrasa, blocking the street and public thoroughfare,” it stated, adding that they were brought under control.

It stated that the Khushab deputy commissioner had imposed a complete ban on gatherings, rallies, processions and protests under Section 144 on November 23. The nominated individuals had violated the order and “incited the crowd by delivering inflammatory speeches”.

Fazl-govt rift

On Tuesday, JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman claimed he had been put under an hours-long “state siege” to restrict his movement.

The JUI-F chief was scheduled to participate in a multiparty conference hosted by the Lahore High Court Bar Association on Tuesday. However, he could not leave his residence in a private housing society on Multan Road due to the deployment of a heavy police contingent.

The development came after tensions persisted between JUI-F and the Centre. Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

JUI-F spokesman Ghouri had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.
